rights.note: An original course on probability, written by the author, with no outside source text. Historical dates (Cardano, Pascal and Fermat, Bernoulli) and every probability figure were checked on 24 Nov 2026; the figures were computed exactly.

ideas.name: The coin has no memory
ideas.can: Explain why long streaks are normal in random sequences and why independent events have no memory.

ideas.name: The birthday surprise
ideas.can: Explain the birthday result by counting pairs, and judge whether a coincidence is really surprising.

ideas.name: Why the casino always wins
ideas.can: Explain the law of large numbers and why a small edge becomes a near certainty over many trials.

ideas.name: When a positive test misleads
ideas.can: Use a base rate to work out how likely a positive result is to be real, by picturing 1,000 people.

ideas.name: Good bets that lose
ideas.can: Work out expected value by weighing outcomes by their chances, and know when to look beyond it.

ideas.name: Why we fear the wrong things
ideas.can: Translate relative risk into absolute risk and read a scary headline calmly.

lessons.title: Why we fear the wrong things
